symptoms.description: Profuse sweating during the night, which may be severe enough to soak clothing.

symptoms.title: Fatigue
symptoms.description: Tiredness or weakness that does not improve with rest.

symptoms.title: Fever
symptoms.description: A persistent fever without infection can be a sign of NHL.

diagnosis.paragraph: A doctor may feel for enlarged lymph nodes or other signs of lymphoma during a physical examination.
Blood tests can help detect abnormal cell counts or other signs of lymphoma.
A biopsy, often of an enlarged lymph node or other affected tissue, is necessary to confirm the diagnosis of NHL.
Imaging tests such as CT scans, PET scans, and MRIs can help locate the tumor and determine how far the cancer has spread.

options.p: Chemotherapy is the primary treatment for most forms of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma. It uses drugs to destroy cancerous cells or stop their growth.
Radiation therapy uses high-energy rays to target and kill cancer cells, especially in localized NHL cases.
Targeted therapies specifically attack the molecules that contribute to cancer cell growth, often with fewer side effects than chemotherapy.
Immunotherapy works by stimulating the body’s immune system to fight cancer cells or by providing synthetic immune system proteins.
In cases of aggressive NHL, a stem cell transplant may be considered to restore healthy blood cells after chemotherapy or radiation.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for Non-Hodgkin lymphoma depends on the subtype, stage, and overall health of the patient. Some types of NHL are highly treatable, while others are more aggressive.

rows.description: Cancer is localized in a single lymph node or area
Cancer is in multiple lymph nodes or areas on one side of the diaphragm
Cancer has spread to lymph nodes on both sides of the diaphragm
Cancer has spread to other organs, such as the liver, bone marrow, or lungs

heroSection.title: Understanding Oral Cancer
heroSection.description: Learn about oral cancer, which affects the mouth, lips, tongue, gums, and other parts of the oral cavity.

paragraphs: Oral cancer refers to cancer that forms in the tissues of the mouth or throat. It can occur on the lips, tongue, gums, the roof or floor of the mouth, and the lining of the cheeks.
The majority of oral cancers are squamous cell carcinomas, which start in the thin, flat cells that line the oral cavity. It is often linked to tobacco use, alcohol consumption, and HPV infection.

symptoms.title: Sore or Ulcer in the Mouth
symptoms.description: A persistent sore or ulcer that doesn't heal.

symptoms.title: Lumps or Swellings
symptoms.description: Lumps or swelling in the mouth, jaw, or neck.

symptoms.title: Difficulty Swallowing
symptoms.description: Trouble swallowing or a feeling of something stuck in the throat.

symptoms.title: Pain or Tenderness
symptoms.description: Pain or tenderness in the mouth or lips, often when chewing or speaking.

symptoms.title: Changes in Voice
symptoms.description: A hoarse voice or changes in speech may occur.

diagnosis.paragraph: A doctor or dentist inspects the mouth for abnormal growths, sores, or signs of infection.
A biopsy involves taking a tissue sample from a suspicious area to confirm the presence of cancerous cells.
CT scans, MRIs, or PET scans are used to determine if the cancer has spread to other parts of the body.

options.p: Surgical removal of the tumor or affected area is often the first treatment for oral cancer. In some cases, it may involve removing part of the jaw or tongue.
Radiation therapy is used to target cancer cells in the mouth and throat, often after surgery to ensure all cancerous tissue is removed.
Chemotherapy uses powerful drugs to kill cancer cells, and it may be used in conjunction with surgery and radiation for advanced cases.
Targeted therapies can target specific proteins or mutations in cancer cells to stop their growth, and it may be used in some cases of oral cancer.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for oral cancer depends on the stage of the cancer, its location, and how early it is detected. Early-stage oral cancer is often treatable with surgery and radiation.

rows.description: Tumor is ≤ 2 cm and localized to the mouth
Tumor is > 2 cm but still localized
Cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes
Cancer has spread to distant organs or structures

heroSection.title: Understanding Ovarian Cancer
heroSection.description: Ovarian cancer affects the ovaries and is one of the most common types of cancer in women. Learn about causes, symptoms, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Ovarian cancer is cancer that starts in the ovaries, the reproductive glands where eggs are produced. It is often not detected until it has spread within the pelvis and abdomen.
The most common types of ovarian cancer are epithelial ovarian cancers, which arise from the outer layer of the ovary. Genetic mutations, including those in BRCA genes, can increase the risk.

symptoms.title: Abdominal Bloating
symptoms.description: Persistent bloating or feeling full quickly after eating.

symptoms.title: Pelvic or Abdominal Pain
symptoms.description: Pain in the pelvic region or abdomen that is persistent or does not go away.

symptoms.title: Changes in Bowel Habits
symptoms.description: Changes such as constipation, diarrhea, or frequent urination.

symptoms.title: Fatigue
symptoms.description: Unusual or unexplained fatigue or feeling tired all the time.

symptoms.title: Loss of Appetite
symptoms.description: A decrease in appetite, leading to weight loss.

diagnosis.paragraph: A doctor manually examines the ovaries for any abnormal growths or tenderness.
An ultrasound is used to create images of the ovaries to check for abnormalities such as cysts or masses.
The CA-125 test measures the level of a protein in the blood that can be elevated in ovarian cancer.
CT scans or MRI scans are used to determine the extent of the cancer and if it has spread.

options.p: Surgery is the primary treatment for ovarian cancer and often involves removing the ovaries, fallopian tubes, and sometimes the uterus.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cancer cells or stop them from growing. It is often used after surgery to destroy remaining cancer cells.
Targeted therapy aims at specific genes or proteins in cancer cells, blocking the growth and spread of tumors.
Hormone therapy may be used to block the hormones that encourage the growth of certain types of ovarian cancer.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for ovarian cancer depends on the stage at diagnosis, with earlier stages having better outcomes. Unfortunately, ovarian cancer is often diagnosed at later stages.

rows.description: Cancer is confined to one or both ovaries
Cancer has spread to the pelvis
Cancer has spread to the abdomen
Cancer has spread to distant organs

heroSection.title: Understanding Pancreatic Cancer
heroSection.description: Pancreatic cancer starts in the pancreas and is often diagnosed at an advanced stage. Learn about its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Pancreatic cancer begins in the pancreas, a gland located behind the stomach that helps with digestion and blood sugar regulation. It is a highly aggressive cancer with a poor prognosis.
Most pancreatic cancers are exocrine cancers, specifically pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas. Risk factors include smoking, obesity, family history, and certain genetic mutations like BRCA.

symptoms.title: Abdominal Pain
symptoms.description: Pain in the upper abdomen or back, often worsening after eating.

symptoms.title: Unexplained Weight Loss
symptoms.description: Significant weight loss without changing diet or exercise habits.

symptoms.title: Jaundice
symptoms.description: Yellowing of the skin or eyes, a result of a blocked bile duct.

symptoms.title: Fatigue
symptoms.description: Chronic fatigue or weakness, often feeling unusually tired.

symptoms.title: Nausea and Vomiting
symptoms.description: Persistent nausea and vomiting, particularly after eating.

diagnosis.paragraph: CT scans are often used to obtain detailed images of the pancreas and surrounding organs to identify tumors.
A thin tube with an ultrasound device is inserted into the stomach to get a close look at the pancreas and take a biopsy if needed.
MRI scans provide detailed images and help in assessing the spread of cancer in the pancreas.
A blood test can measure levels of CA 19-9, a marker that may be elevated in people with pancreatic cancer.

options.p: Surgery may be an option if the cancer is localized and hasn't spread. The Whipple procedure is the most common surgery for pancreatic cancer.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to target cancer cells. It's often used before surgery to shrink tumors or after surgery to kill remaining cancer cells.
Radiation therapy uses high-energy beams to kill cancer cells. It may be combined with chemotherapy to treat pancreatic cancer.
Targeted therapy targets specific molecules involved in the growth and spread of cancer cells. This treatment can be used in advanced cases.

prognosisSection.paragraph: Pancreatic cancer has a low survival rate due to its late-stage diagnosis and aggressive nature. Early detection is key to improving outcomes.

rows.description: Cancer is confined to the pancreas
Cancer has spread to nearby tissues or lymph nodes
Cancer has spread to major blood vessels or distant organs
Cancer has spread to distant organs, such as the liver or lungs

heroSection.title: Understanding Penile Cancer
heroSection.description: Penile cancer is a rare cancer that affects the tissues of the penis. Learn about its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Penile cancer is a type of cancer that occurs in the tissues of the penis. It often starts in the skin cells of the penis and can spread to other parts of the body if not treated early.

The most common type of penile cancer is squamous cell carcinoma. Risk factors include smoking, human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, poor hygiene, and a history of certain sexually transmitted infections.

symptoms.title: Lump or Growth on the Penis
symptoms.description: A lump or growth that may be painless initially, but could become painful as the cancer progresses.

symptoms.title: Changes in the Skin
symptoms.description: Changes such as color changes, thickening, or sores that do not heal.

symptoms.title: Pain or Discomfort
symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort in the penis, particularly in the area where the cancer is located.

symptoms.title: Swelling or Enlarged Lymph Nodes
symptoms.description: Swelling in the groin area due to the spread of cancer to the lymph nodes.

symptoms.title: Unusual Discharge
symptoms.description: Unusual discharge or bleeding from the penis, sometimes with an unpleasant odor.

diagnosis.paragraph: The doctor will conduct a physical exam to check for visible lumps, growths, or any abnormalities on the penis.
A tissue sample is taken from the lump or lesion for laboratory examination to confirm the presence of cancer.
An ultrasound may be used to check for cancer spread to nearby lymph nodes or other tissues.
A CT scan may be performed to determine if cancer has spread to other parts of the body.

options.p: Surgery is the most common treatment for penile cancer. It may involve the removal of the tumor, part of the penis, or the entire penis in severe cases.
Radiation therapy uses high-energy rays to kill cancer cells. It may be used after surgery or as an alternative if surgery is not possible.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cancer cells or stop their growth. It may be used for advanced cases or to shrink tumors before surgery.
In some cases, topical treatments such as imiquimod or 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) may be used to treat early-stage penile cancer.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for penile cancer depends on the stage of the cancer at diagnosis. Early detection is critical for successful treatment and better outcomes.

rows.description: Tumor confined to the penis, no lymph node involvement
Cancer has spread to nearby tissues or lymph nodes
Cancer has spread to regional lymph nodes
Cancer has spread to distant organs or lymph nodes

heroSection.title: Understanding Pituitary Tumors
heroSection.description: Pituitary tumors are abnormal growths in the pituitary gland, which controls critical body functions. Learn about their causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Pituitary tumors are growths that develop in the pituitary gland, a small gland located at the base of the brain. While most pituitary tumors are benign (non-cancerous), they can still cause a variety of symptoms due to their location and impact on hormone production.

Pituitary tumors can interfere with the gland’s ability to produce hormones, leading to various symptoms depending on the type of hormone affected. They may also exert pressure on surrounding structures, such as the optic nerves, leading to vision problems.

symptoms.title: Headaches
symptoms.description: Frequent or persistent headaches, often caused by pressure from the tumor on nearby structures.

symptoms.title: Vision Problems
symptoms.description: Loss of peripheral vision or double vision due to pressure on the optic nerves.

symptoms.title: Hormonal Imbalances
symptoms.description: Changes in hormone levels that can lead to a variety of symptoms, including fatigue, weight gain, or changes in menstrual cycles.

symptoms.title: Fatigue
symptoms.description: Extreme tiredness or weakness due to hormonal imbalances caused by the tumor.

symptoms.title: Nausea and Vomiting
symptoms.description: A result of increased pressure in the brain from a large tumor or its hormonal effects.

diagnosis.paragraph: The doctor will conduct a thorough physical exam, looking for signs of hormonal imbalance and changes in vision.
An MRI scan provides detailed images of the pituitary gland and surrounding structures to identify tumors.
A CT scan may be used to provide additional detail or if an MRI is not available.
Blood tests help measure hormone levels and can identify whether the pituitary gland is producing too much or too little of a particular hormone.

options.p: Surgery to remove the tumor is often the first-line treatment, especially for tumors that are causing significant symptoms or hormone imbalances. Most tumors are accessed through the nose via endoscopic surgery.
Radiation therapy is used when surgery is not an option or to treat remaining tumor cells after surgery.
Medications, including dopamine agonists, somatostatin analogs, and corticosteroids, can be used to shrink tumors or correct hormone imbalances.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for pituitary tumors depends on factors such as tumor size, location, and the extent of hormonal imbalance. Most patients with benign pituitary tumors can expect a good long-term outlook with treatment.

rows.description: Small tumor, confined to the pituitary gland
Moderate tumor size, localized
Tumor affecting surrounding structures or spreading
Aggressive or metastatic tumors

heroSection.title: Understanding Prostate Cancer
heroSection.description: Prostate cancer is one of the most common types of cancer among men. Learn about its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Prostate cancer is a type of cancer that begins in the prostate gland, a small walnut-shaped gland that produces seminal fluid. The cancer typically grows slowly, but in some cases, it can be aggressive and spread to other parts of the body.
Most prostate cancers are adenocarcinomas, which develop in the gland cells. Risk factors include age, family history, race, and lifestyle choices, with older men being at higher risk.

symptoms.title: Difficulty Urinating
symptoms.description: A feeling of incomplete emptying or weak urine flow, often due to the tumor pressing on the urethra.

symptoms.title: Blood in Urine or Semen
symptoms.description: Blood in urine or semen can sometimes be a sign of prostate cancer.

symptoms.title: Pain in the Lower Back, Hips, or Thighs
symptoms.description: Persistent pain or discomfort in these areas, which can be a sign of cancer spreading to nearby bones.

symptoms.title: Erectile Dysfunction
symptoms.description: Difficulty achieving or maintaining an erection, which can be linked to prostate cancer.

symptoms.title: Painful Ejaculation
symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort during ejaculation.

diagnosis.paragraph: A healthcare provider manually examines the prostate for lumps or abnormalities through the rectum.
A blood test that measures the level of PSA, a substance produced by the prostate. Elevated PSA levels can indicate prostate cancer or other prostate conditions.
A tissue sample is taken from the prostate for examination under a microscope to confirm the presence of cancer.
These imaging techniques can help determine the size and spread of the tumor.

options.p: Radical prostatectomy, the surgical removal of the prostate gland, is a common treatment for localized prostate cancer.
Radiation therapy uses high-energy rays to target and kill cancer cells. It may be used after surgery or for more advanced cases.
Hormone therapy reduces the levels of male hormones (androgens) that fuel prostate cancer growth. It is often used in advanced stages.
Chemotherapy may be used for advanced or metastatic prostate cancer that doesn't respond to other treatments.
For low-risk, slow-growing prostate cancer, active surveillance may be recommended, with regular monitoring rather than immediate treatment.

prognosisSection.paragraph: Prostate cancer typically grows slowly, and many men live for many years after diagnosis, especially with early detection and treatment. The survival rate is high for localized prostate cancer.

rows.description: Localized to the prostate, not spread
Localized but larger tumor size
Spread to nearby tissues or lymph nodes
Distant metastasis

heroSection.title: Understanding Salivary Gland Cancer
heroSection.description: Salivary gland cancer is a rare type of cancer that starts in the glands that produce saliva. Learn about the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Salivary gland cancer occurs in the salivary glands, which are responsible for producing saliva. This cancer can develop in any of the major or minor salivary glands. It's relatively rare compared to other cancers.
Most salivary gland cancers are adenocarcinomas, which are cancers that originate in glandular cells. Risk factors include radiation exposure and certain inherited conditions.

symptoms.title: Swelling or Lump in the Mouth or Neck
symptoms.description: A painless lump or swelling near the jaw or in the neck, which is one of the most common symptoms.

symptoms.title: Pain in the Affected Area
symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort near the jaw, mouth, or neck, particularly when swallowing or chewing.

symptoms.title: Difficulty Swallowing
symptoms.description: Pain or difficulty swallowing, often accompanied by a feeling of fullness.

symptoms.title: Numbness or Weakness in the Face
symptoms.description: A feeling of numbness or weakness in the muscles of the face on one side.

symptoms.title: Dry Mouth
symptoms.description: A decrease in saliva production, leading to dry mouth or difficulty speaking.

diagnosis.paragraph: A doctor will check for swelling or lumps in the mouth, neck, and face and may perform a thorough head and neck exam.
CT scans, MRIs, and ultrasounds are commonly used to determine the size, location, and spread of the tumor.
A sample of the tumor tissue is removed and examined under a microscope to confirm the presence of cancer cells.

options.p: Surgical removal of the tumor and possibly the affected salivary gland is the primary treatment for most cases of salivary gland cancer.
Radiation therapy may be used after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells or if the tumor is inoperable.
Chemotherapy may be recommended in advanced cases of salivary gland cancer, especially if the cancer has spread to other areas of the body.

prognosisSection.paragraph: Prognosis depends on the type and stage of salivary gland cancer. Most people with early-stage salivary gland cancer have a favorable outcome, but the prognosis may vary based on factors such as tumor size and location.

rows.description: Localized tumor, small in size
Tumor larger but still confined
Spread to nearby lymph nodes
Distant metastasis

heroSection.title: Understanding Skin Cancer
heroSection.description: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer, and it forms in the skin cells. Learn about the causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Skin cancer occurs when abnormal cells begin to grow uncontrollably in the skin. It is the most common type of cancer in the world and can occur in any part of the body.

The three main types of skin cancer are basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma. Basal cell and squamous cell cancers are common but rarely spread, while melanoma can spread to other parts of the body.

symptoms.title: New Growth or Mole
symptoms.description: A new growth or an existing mole that changes in size, shape, or color.

symptoms.title: Itchy or Painful Spot
symptoms.description: An area of the skin that becomes itchy, painful, or tender.

symptoms.title: Bleeding or Oozing
symptoms.description: A mole or growth that begins to bleed or ooze, especially if it wasn't injured.

symptoms.title: Irregular Borders
symptoms.description: Moles or spots with uneven borders, which are characteristic of melanoma.

symptoms.title: Color Variation
symptoms.description: A spot or mole that has different colors within it, such as shades of brown, black, and even red or white.

diagnosis.paragraph: A dermatologist will visually examine your skin for signs of abnormal growths or changes in existing moles.
A sample of the suspicious skin tissue is removed and analyzed to determine if cancer cells are present.
In some cases, imaging tests like CT scans or MRIs may be used to check if the cancer has spread to other areas.

options.p: Surgical excision is the most common treatment for skin cancer, involving removal of the tumor and surrounding tissue.
Radiation therapy may be used for cancers that are difficult to remove surgically or if they have spread.
Certain skin cancers can be treated with topical treatments such as creams that target cancer cells directly on the skin.
Chemotherapy is used for advanced skin cancers, particularly melanoma, when the cancer has spread beyond the skin.

prognosisSection.paragraph: Skin cancer prognosis depends on the type, size, and location of the tumor. Basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma typically have very high cure rates when detected early. Melanoma can be more aggressive, but it has a good survival rate when caught early.

rows.description: Localized to the skin
Tumor grows larger or spreads to nearby tissue
Spread to lymph nodes
Distant metastasis

heroSection.title: Understanding Stomach Cancer
heroSection.description: Stomach cancer, also known as gastric cancer, occurs when cancer cells form in the lining of the stomach. Explore its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Stomach cancer, or gastric cancer, begins in the stomach lining. It can develop in various parts of the stomach and may spread to nearby organs.

The exact cause of stomach cancer is not fully understood, but risk factors include infection with Helicobacter pylori, a family history of stomach cancer, smoking, and a diet high in salty and smoked foods.

symptoms.title: Persistent Stomach Pain
symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort in the stomach area, often after eating.

symptoms.title: Bloating or Fullness
symptoms.description: Feeling full after eating even a small amount of food.

symptoms.title: Nausea and Vomiting
symptoms.description: Nausea or vomiting, sometimes with blood.

symptoms.title: Unexplained Weight Loss
symptoms.description: Losing weight without trying, due to difficulty eating or nutrient absorption.

symptoms.title: Difficulty Swallowing
symptoms.description: Difficulty swallowing food, especially solid foods.

diagnosis.paragraph: A flexible tube is used to examine the stomach lining for abnormalities and take tissue samples for biopsy.
A series of X-rays are taken after the patient drinks a contrast liquid to highlight the stomach and detect abnormal growths.
Tissue samples are taken during an endoscopy to determine if cancer cells are present.
Imaging tests such as CT or PET scans help determine the extent of the cancer and whether it has spread.

options.p: Surgical removal of the tumor is the primary treatment, and in some cases, the entire stomach may be removed.
Chemotherapy is often used before or after surgery to shrink the tumor or eliminate remaining cancer cells.
Radiation therapy may be used to treat stomach cancer, especially when it is inoperable or has spread to other organs.
Targeted drugs are used to target specific molecules involved in cancer growth and spread.

prognosisSection.paragraph: Stomach cancer prognosis depends on the stage at diagnosis and the effectiveness of treatments. Early-stage stomach cancer has a better chance of survival compared to advanced stages.

rows.description: Cancer confined to the stomach lining
Spread to nearby lymph nodes
Cancer has spread to nearby organs
Distant metastasis

heroSection.title: Understanding Uterine Cancer
heroSection.description: Uterine cancer, also known as endometrial cancer, begins in the lining of the uterus. Learn about its causes, symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment options.

paragraphs: Uterine cancer is cancer that begins in the uterus, specifically in the lining known as the endometrium. It is one of the most common cancers of the female reproductive system.

The exact cause of uterine cancer is not fully known, but factors like obesity, hormone replacement therapy, and certain genetic conditions increase the risk. It typically occurs in postmenopausal women, but it can affect younger women as well.

symptoms.title: Abnormal Vaginal Bleeding
symptoms.description: The most common symptom is bleeding that is not part of the regular menstrual cycle, especially after menopause.

symptoms.title: Pelvic Pain
symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort in the pelvic area, which may worsen over time.

symptoms.title: Pain During Urination or Intercourse
symptoms.description: Painful urination or pain during sexual activity.

symptoms.title: Unexplained Weight Loss
symptoms.description: Weight loss that occurs without trying, which can be a sign of advanced disease.

diagnosis.paragraph: A doctor may conduct a pelvic exam to feel for any abnormalities or masses in the uterus or surrounding areas.
An ultrasound is used to examine the uterus and detect abnormal growths or changes in the lining.
A sample of the endometrial tissue is taken to check for cancer cells.
A small, lighted camera is inserted through the cervix to examine the inside of the uterus and take a biopsy if needed.
Imaging tests help determine the size and spread of the tumor, if present.

options.p: The main treatment for uterine cancer is surgery, typically a hysterectomy to remove the uterus, and sometimes the ovaries and fallopian tubes.
Radiation therapy may be used to treat localized tumors or to reduce the risk of recurrence after surgery.
Chemotherapy may be used in more advanced stages to destroy cancer cells that have spread beyond the uterus.
Hormone therapy, such as progestins, can be used to treat cancers that are estrogen receptor-positive.

prognosisSection.paragraph: The prognosis for uterine cancer depends on the stage at diagnosis and the success of treatment. Early detection leads to higher survival rates.

rows.description: Cancer confined to the uterus
Spread to the cervix
Spread to nearby tissues or lymph nodes
Distant metastasis

alok.name: Dr. Alok Tiwari
alok.qualification: Chief Surgical Oncologist, MBBS (Gold Medalist), MS (Gen Surgery) KGMU Lucknow, DNB, Dip MAS, daVinciXi Certified Robotic Onco Surgeon, Surgical Oncology, ESSO (Breast Oncoplasty), FMAS, FALS (Colorectal)
alok.greeting: Welcome to Synergy Super Speciality Hospital & Cancer Institute.
message: Healthcare is not merely about treating diseases—it is about restoring hope, protecting dignity, and transforming lives. Every patient who walks through our doors entrusts us with something invaluable: their faith. At Synergy, we consider that trust our greatest responsibility.

When we established Synergy in 2023, our vision extended far beyond building another hospital. We envisioned creating a centre of excellence where advanced technology, clinical expertise, ethical medical practice, and compassionate care work together to provide the best possible outcomes for every patient. Today, that vision continues to guide every decision we make.

As a Surgical Oncologist, I have witnessed the emotional, physical, and financial challenges that cancer brings to patients and their families. These experiences strengthened my belief that no patient should lose hope because of cancer, and no family should be denied quality treatment because of financial limitations.

At Synergy, we have built an integrated ecosystem of care that combines Surgical Oncology, Medical Oncology, Radiation Oncology, Pediatric Oncology, Critical Care, Trauma Services, and multiple super-specialty departments under one roof. Our multidisciplinary approach ensures that every patient receives personalized, evidence-based treatment supported by the latest medical technology and internationally accepted clinical protocols.

Our aspiration goes beyond the walls of our hospital. We are committed to making quality healthcare accessible across Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Western Bihar, and Southern Nepal through our expanding network of peripheral centres, community outreach programs, cancer awareness initiatives, early detection services, and preventive healthcare campaigns. We firmly believe that early diagnosis, timely intervention, and patient education can save thousands of lives.

vision.title: My Dream
vision.text: To build a future where no family in Purvanchal, Western Bihar, or Southern Nepal loses a loved one because cancer was diagnosed too late, quality treatment was inaccessible, or financial hardship became a barrier to care.

commitment: This mission inspires every member of the Synergy family to work with compassion, integrity, innovation, and excellence every single day.

The journey of healthcare never stands still. We will continue investing in advanced technologies, robotic surgery, radiation oncology, academic excellence, research, digital healthcare, and highly skilled professionals so that our patients receive treatment comparable to the finest healthcare institutions in the country.

On behalf of our entire team, I sincerely thank every patient, family member, healthcare professional, and well-wisher for placing their trust in Synergy. Your confidence motivates us to continuously raise the standards of healthcare and pursue excellence without compromise.
Together, let us build a healthier future—where hope triumphs over fear, compassion overcomes suffering, and quality healthcare reaches every individual who needs it.
alok.organization: Synergy Super Speciality Hospital & Cancer Institute

As Medical Director & CEO, my commitment is to ensure that every department, every healthcare professional, and every process works together with one common purpose—to place the patient at the centre of everything we do.

We continuously invest in advanced medical technology, highly skilled professionals, evidence-based clinical practices, and internationally recognized quality standards to ensure that our patients receive safe, effective, and personalized treatment. Every milestone we achieve reflects our unwavering commitment to excellence and continuous improvement.

Our responsibility extends beyond the hospital campus. We are dedicated to expanding access to advanced healthcare across Purvanchal, Western Bihar, and Southern Nepal through specialized services, peripheral centres, preventive healthcare initiatives, early diagnosis programs, and community outreach. We believe that quality healthcare should be accessible to every individual, regardless of geography or socioeconomic status.

commitment: This vision inspires every member of the Synergy family to uphold the values of compassion, integrity, accountability, and excellence in every interaction and every decision.

Healthcare is constantly evolving, and so are we. We remain committed to embracing innovation, strengthening our clinical services, enhancing patient experience, and setting new benchmarks in quality healthcare for the communities we proudly serve.
On behalf of our entire team, I sincerely thank our patients, their families, our dedicated healthcare professionals, and our well-wishers for their continued trust and confidence.
Together, we will continue building a healthier future founded on excellence, compassion, and hope.

hero.title: Prevent Cancer Before It Starts
hero.subtitle: Small lifestyle changes today can make a world of difference tomorrow.

intro.title: Why Cancer Prevention Matters
intro.description: Prevention is the most powerful tool we have against cancer. From lifestyle choices to regular screenings, there are many ways to lower your risk and protect your long-term health.

tips.title: Avoid Tobacco
tips.description: Smoking and tobacco use are the leading causes of cancer. Quitting significantly reduces your risk.

tips.title: Eat a Healthy Diet
tips.description: Include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins. Reduce processed foods and red meats.

tips.title: Stay Active & Maintain Weight
tips.description: Obesity is linked to many cancers. Aim for regular physical activity and a balanced diet.

tips.title: Limit Alcohol
tips.description: If you drink, do so in moderation. Excessive alcohol increases the risk of several cancers.

tips.title: Protect from Sun Exposure
tips.description: Use sunscreen, wear protective clothing, and avoid tanning beds to reduce skin cancer risk.

tips.title: Get Vaccinated
tips.description: Vaccines like HPV and Hepatitis B can prevent infections that may lead to cancer.

tips.title: Schedule Regular Screenings
tips.description: Routine checkups and screenings can detect cancer early when treatment is most effective.

hero.title: Cancer Diagnosis & Staging
hero.subtitle: Early detection is the first step to effective treatment. Here's how the process works.

intro.title: Understanding the Process
intro.description: Accurate diagnosis and cancer staging are crucial to determining the right treatment plan and improving outcomes. Each step ensures clarity and personalized care.

stages.title: Initial Consultation & Medical History
stages.description: Your physician begins with a detailed discussion about symptoms, lifestyle, and family history to identify possible cancer risks.

stages.title: Physical Examination
stages.description: A thorough physical check-up helps detect visible abnormalities or lumps that may require further testing.

stages.title: Diagnostic Imaging
stages.description: Technologies such as CT, MRI, PET scans, and X-rays help identify tumors and determine their size and location.

stages.title: Biopsy & Lab Tests
stages.description: Tissue samples are examined under a microscope to confirm the presence and type of cancer.

stages.title: Cancer Staging
stages.description: Staging defines how much the cancer has grown or spread. It helps guide treatment options and prognosis.

stages.title: Molecular & Genetic Testing
stages.description: Advanced tests identify mutations or markers that can help with personalized treatment plans.

hero.title: Cancer Treatment Options
hero.subtitle: Discover the latest and most effective treatment methods available today.

intro.title: Personalized Cancer Care
intro.description: Cancer treatment is tailored to the type, stage, and genetics of the disease, as well as your health and preferences. Learn about each major option available.

treatments.title: Surgery
treatments.description: Physically removes the tumor from the body. Often used when cancer is localized and hasn’t spread.

treatments.title: Radiation Therapy
treatments.description: Uses high-energy rays to kill cancer cells or shrink tumors. Can be external or internal.

treatments.title: Chemotherapy
treatments.description: Involves powerful drugs that target and destroy rapidly dividing cancer cells.

treatments.title: Targeted Therapy
treatments.description: Uses drugs to target specific genes or proteins involved in cancer growth.

treatments.title: Immunotherapy
treatments.description: Helps your immune system recognize and fight cancer more effectively.

treatments.title: Hormone Therapy
treatments.description: Blocks or removes hormones that fuel certain cancers like breast and prostate cancer.

hero.title: Nutrition & Wellness in Cancer Care
hero.subtitle: Nourishing your body and mind before, during, and after cancer treatment.

intro.title: The Power of Nutrition & Healthy Living
intro.description: Proper nutrition and holistic wellness play a critical role in strengthening your immune system, managing side effects, and supporting recovery throughout your cancer journey.

tips.title: Eat Plant-Based Meals
tips.description: Incorporate more vegetables, fruits, legumes, and whole grains to support your immune system and reduce cancer risk.

tips.title: Stay Hydrated
tips.description: Drink plenty of water throughout the day to support digestion, detoxification, and cellular health.

tips.title: Avoid Processed Foods
tips.description: Limit intake of processed meats, sugary drinks, and refined grains to reduce inflammation and maintain healthy weight.

tips.title: Exercise Regularly
tips.description: Engage in physical activity like walking, yoga, or strength training for at least 30 minutes most days of the week.

tips.title: Prioritize Sleep
tips.description: Aim for 7–9 hours of quality sleep to enhance immune function and reduce stress.
